title: Royal Navy Submariner Recruitment 2026
metaDescription: Royal Navy submariner recruitment 2026: entry ages 16-39, 10 weeks at HMS Raleigh, earning your dolphins, submarine pay and life on board explained.
headline: Royal Navy Submariner Recruitment 2026

sections.title: Who can join as a submariner?
sections.content:
Royal Navy submariners are volunteers from within the Royal Navy: you first join as a rating or officer in a relevant branch, such as warfare, engineering or logistics, and then volunteer for submarine service. General entry for ratings starts at age 16 with parental consent under 18, and most roles accept applicants up to age 39.

All submariner candidates must pass the standard Royal Navy medical, fitness and security checks, plus additional submarine-specific medical screening. Life underwater demands good hearing, dental fitness and psychological resilience, so the medical bar is deliberately thorough.

sections.title: Training: from Raleigh to the boat
sections.content:
Every rating begins with 10 weeks of basic training at HMS Raleigh in Cornwall, covering military skills, seamanship, firefighting and damage control. After that, submariners complete specialist branch training and then submarine qualification training, learning how a boat's systems work before their first sea draft.

New submariners join a boat as trainees and earn their dolphins, the submarine qualification badge, by demonstrating knowledge of every major system on board. Only after qualifying do they count as fully fledged submariners, and the process typically takes several months at sea.

sections.title: Life on board a submarine
sections.content:
Submarine life is unlike any other naval job: crews work in shifts around the clock, share cramped cabins, and can spend weeks submerged without daylight or fresh air. Patrols on ballistic missile submarines can last around three months, while attack submarines deploy for shorter but still demanding periods.

The trade-off is close camaraderie, extra submarine pay on top of normal naval pay, and accelerated responsibility. Submariners often qualify for additional allowances and faster promotion than their surface-fleet counterparts, reflecting the demands of the role.

sections.title: Career paths and prospects
sections.content:
Submariners can progress from able rate to leading hand, petty officer and beyond, or commission as officers through promotion routes. Engineering submariners are especially sought after, with nuclear engineering skills that transfer well to civilian power and defence industries after service.

The Royal Navy is renewing its submarine fleet, including the Dreadnought-class ballistic missile submarines, so demand for submariners is expected to stay strong through the late 2020s. For applicants who want the most distinctive role in the Navy, the Submarine Service is the clear choice.

faqs.q: How old do you have to be to join the Royal Navy Submarine Service?
faqs.a: Royal Navy ratings can generally join from age 16, with parental consent required under 18, and most roles accept applicants up to age 39. Submariners are volunteers from within the Navy, so you join a relevant branch first and then volunteer for submarine service after basic training.

faqs.q: How long is Royal Navy basic training?
faqs.a: Basic training for ratings lasts 10 weeks at HMS Raleigh in Cornwall. It covers military skills, seamanship, firefighting and damage control. After Raleigh, submariners complete specialist branch training and submarine qualification training before joining a boat as trainees. Trainees then learn their specialist branch skills before joining their first boat and working toward qualification.

faqs.q: What are dolphins in the Royal Navy?
faqs.a: Dolphins are the submarine qualification badge, earned by demonstrating working knowledge of every major system on board a submarine. New joiners serve as trainees on their first boat and only count as qualified submariners once they have earned their dolphins, which typically takes several months at sea.

Yes, submariners receive additional submarine pay on top of normal Royal Navy pay, plus allowances that reflect the demands of the role. Combined with faster promotion in many branches, this makes the Submarine Service one of the better-paid paths for ratings in the Royal Navy.
